_what_this_is: The manifest for the insurance body of work. gen_insurance.py builds the hub from it and REFUSES to build when it disagrees with the folder: a doctrine document declared here with no file, a src/*.md nothing declares, an MVP folder that does not exist, or a memo marked processed with no brief. The count on the hub is computed from this file, never typed.
_authority: NONE — a build input. The briefs under /briefs/ and the markdown under src/ are the sources of truth.

stage.why: A rating engine that emits levels rather than currency is not a regulated activity, needs no carrier and no loss history, and is therefore buildable today. Money is stage 2. See GM-D38.
stage.rule: A level nobody can recompute is exactly the theatre a premium would have prevented. Every rating ships its derivation. See GM-D39.

memos.note: The project lead is recording eight memos on this pivot. Each is filed verbatim as a brief before it is read; the doctrine below is derived from them and says which memo it came from. A memo not yet recorded is listed as awaited rather than guessed at.

items.title: The pivot briefing: the delta is where the insurance lives
items.gave: The policy replaces the acceptance at the foundation; the insurer as the acceptor of last resort filling the register's acceptor:null; the two-insurances split; parametric as the payout shape; the loss event named as the missing primitive.

items.title: Insurance without money first: the rating is the product
items.gave: Money decoupled from rating, which dissolves the regulatory blocker; micro-policies as the scale insurance never reached; the placement variables; the questionnaire as a declared-fact collector; the quasi-currency as the adoption path. Also contradicts memo 0 on why the pivot is honest, and the contradiction is answered rather than smoothed.

doctrine.title: What this is, and the rule it runs on
doctrine.one_line: The body of work, its two stages, and the one rule that keeps a rating from becoming theatre.

doctrine.title: The rating: what is scored, from what evidence, and what must never merge
doctrine.one_line: The ratable unit is a placement, not an agent; inputs carry their evidence channel; measured and declared never merge; unknown is never absent.

does_not_prove: That any of this is insurance. Stage 1 emits a rating, transfers no risk, and promises no payout — which is exactly why it needs no carrier and why calling it insurance would be the first dishonesty.

That the placement orderings are true. Claude-on-a-desktop is rated higher than Claude-on-the-web in the project lead's judgement; nobody has measured a desktop agent, so the estate cannot score its own leading example.
That a level means the same thing to two organisations. Nothing here is calibrated against loss data, because no agent loss data exists anywhere.
That aggregation works yet. Correlated risk is named as a graph problem and not solved; summing micro ratings would be wrong in the dangerous direction.
